segments.flavor: the sign on the door
segments.text:
Ivy: [whisper] Study Hall. Open all night. The lamps are on and nobody is going to bother you.
Ivy: Stay as long as you need. The record is still going.

segments.flavor: the sign on the door, shorter
segments.text: Ivy: [gentle] Study Hall, all night, every night. Put the chair back when you leave. Here's the music.

segments.flavor: the whole handbook
segments.text:
Ivy: This is Study Hall. Two rules. Keep it quiet, and finish the sentence you started.
Ivy: [whisper] That is the whole handbook. Back to the record.

segments.flavor: the station id with a forecast under it
segments.text:
June: [gentle] Study Hall. Marlow Bay tonight is fog, mostly, with a long calm over the harbor.
Ivy: And inside, warm. Nothing due for hours.
June: Nothing at all. Roll the next one.

segments.flavor: Ivy whispers one reminder — the water
segments.text:
Ivy: [whisper] One reminder, then I will be quiet. The glass beside the mug is still full.
Ivy: Drink half of it. This next one is long, and it will wait. Here it comes.

segments.flavor: June reads the overnight forecast for Marlow Bay
segments.text:
June: [gentle] Marlow Bay overnight. Fog on the harbor, thick enough to lean on, thinning by the causeway.
Ivy: And in the reading room?
June: Mild. Still. A ninety percent chance of somebody falling asleep on the long table. Back to the music.

segments.flavor: back-announce like a book placed gently back on the shelf
segments.text:
Ivy: [whisper] That was the one with the rain inside it. I am putting it back on the shelf now.
June: Spine out?
Ivy: Spine out. Third shelf, where the tall books live.
June: [gentle] Good. Take the next one down gently; the cover is loose and the ending is soft.
Ivy: It is already open at the right page. Listen with me.

segments.flavor: a library object the station would sell you a better one of
segments.text:
Ivy: The third desk by the window wobbles. It has wobbled since before either of us worked nights.
June: Someone folded a library card under one leg.
Ivy: A folded card under the short leg. It held for a week, then the card gave up.
June: [gentle] We could buy a desk that does not move.
Ivy: We could. But then what would we talk about at four in the morning.
June: Fair. Nothing changes tonight. The next song does not wobble at all; let it in.

segments.flavor: Theo whispers in about the essay due at dawn
segments.text:
Theo: [whisper] Ivy. It is Theo. I am under the stairs in the stacks, whispering, because someone shushed me.
Ivy: We know the one. That stairwell has heard a lot of essays. How long do you have?
Theo: Six hours. Eleven pages. Zero sentences. I have a title and a lot of courage.
Ivy: Write this down. The first sentence only has to be true, not good.
June: [gentle] And it can be short. Shorter than a forecast, and a forecast is only two sentences.
Theo: True, not good. Short. Okay. Okay. I can do that.
Ivy: Good. Put the phone down and do not call back until page twelve.
June: [whisper] Go gently, Theo. We will keep the music on for you.

segments.flavor: Ivy whispers one reminder — the shoulders
segments.text:
Ivy: [whisper] Posture, and then I will leave it alone. The shoulders have climbed toward the ears again.
Ivy: Let them fall, unclench the jaw, drop the elbows, and give the next four minutes to the piano.

segments.flavor: June reads the overnight forecast for Marlow Bay
segments.text:
June: [gentle] Overnight in Marlow Bay. A light rain on the fish market, moving slowly toward the canal.
Ivy: Slowly how?
June: Slower than the rain wants. It will arrive by morning and apologize for the noise.
Ivy: [whisper] The harbor?
June: Flat as a desk. Nothing moving out there except the bell on the breakwater.
Ivy: Then we are clear until dawn. Something with rain in it, please.

segments.flavor: back-announce like a book placed gently back on the shelf
segments.text:
Ivy: That one had tape hiss all the way under it, like a radiator in another room.
June: I thought that was our radiator.
Ivy: [chuckle] It might have been both. Either way, it is going back on the shelf now.
June: Careful with the corner.
Ivy: Always. Down, flat, spine aligned, and the shelf will never know that it left the room.
June: [gentle] Beautiful. Now pull something with a little dust on it and start the next hour.

segments.flavor: a library object the station would sell you a better one of
segments.text:
Ivy: There are nine coat hooks by the door. Eight of them hold nothing at all.
June: And the ninth?
Ivy: A grey scarf. It has hung there long enough to be considered a fixture.
June: [gentle] We could put a small sign under it. Something kind.
Ivy: What would the sign say?
June: It would say, we are not asking for it back, we are only curious.
Ivy: [whisper] That is too many words for a sign, and exactly right for a scarf.
June: [gentle] It is warm, at least. A scarf on a hook is still a scarf.
Ivy: Nobody claims a scarf in the dark. They walk past it every night.
June: We will write it in the morning. For now, the music, before either of us gets sentimental.

segments.flavor: Theo whispers in about the essay due at dawn
segments.text:
Theo: [whisper] It is Theo. The essay is due at dawn and I have written the title.
Ivy: How is the title?
Theo: ... it is bold.
Ivy: A bold title is a promise. Go and keep it. Music, quietly.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a library product — a chair that does not creak
segments.text:
Ivy: [gentle] Study Hall is brought to you tonight by the Hush Chair, from the Marlow Bay Chair Company.
June: One chair. Four legs. No opinion.
Ivy: The Hush Chair does not creak, does not roll, and does not wake the person beside you.
June: It arrives flat and stays flat until assembled by someone patient.
Ivy: The Hush Chair. Sit in it for six hours and feel almost nothing.
June: [whisper] Chair not responsible for what you do while sitting in it. The music, please.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a library product — a lamp with one setting
segments.text:
June: [gentle] A word about the Third Shelf Lamp, from the people who make almost nothing else.
Ivy: One switch. One brightness. The correct one.
June: It does not dim, pulse, change colour, or ask anything of the room.
Ivy: [whisper] It makes a small circle of light the size of an open book.
June: The Third Shelf Lamp. Warm, steady, and entirely uninterested in your mood.
Ivy: Sold in libraries, mostly to librarians.
June: [whisper] Bulb not included, shade sold separately, lamp does not do homework. Music now.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a library product — a tea that stays warm
segments.text:
Ivy: [gentle] Tonight's break is supported by the Nightwatch Flask. Steel outside. Steel inside. Nothing to argue with.
June: It holds one litre of anything hot for eleven hours.
Ivy: Eleven hours is longer than any night in this building, and we have measured that.
June: The lid seals without a sound, which matters here more than anywhere.
Ivy: The Nightwatch Flask. Warm at four in the morning, warm at six.
June: [whisper] Flask cannot make you drink from it. That part remains yours. Here comes the music.

segments.flavor: the book nobody has returned
segments.text:
Ivy: [gentle] Library notice. The overdue shelf has one permanent resident, and we speak of it kindly.
June: Focus, Finally. Borrowed once. Never returned.
Ivy: It has been out so long that the card in the back is a historical document.
June: [gentle] We are not angry.
Ivy: We are not angry. We would simply like to know whether it worked.
June: Did the focus arrive?
Ivy: [whisper] Did it finally? Leave it on the step if so. No questions. On with the record.

segments.flavor: Ivy's cold tea, reported hourly
segments.text:
June: [gentle] It is time for the tea report. Ivy, what is the temperature of the mug?
Ivy: Room.
June: It was hot at the top of the hour.
Ivy: It was hot at the top of the hour. Then I said one sentence about fog.
June: [chuckle] One sentence.
Ivy: One long sentence. The tea has never survived a forecast, not once, in all these years.
June: I will make you another one.
Ivy: You will, and it will go cold, and that is the arrangement. Play something warm.

segments.flavor: June's forecast for the reading room
segments.text:
June: [gentle] And now the indoor forecast, which we take as seriously as the outdoor one.
Ivy: The reading room, floor by floor.
June: Ground floor, warm, with a draught near the door that nobody has ever located.
Ivy: [whisper] I have looked. It comes from inside the building.
June: Second floor, steady. Third floor, colder, with a seventy percent chance of a borrowed cardigan.
Ivy: And the archives?
June: [gentle] The archives are their own country. Bring a coat and a reason to be there.
Ivy: That concludes the indoor forecast. The next song is a warm one.

segments.flavor: Ivy whispers one reminder — save the file
segments.text:
Ivy: [whisper] Save the file. Not at the end of the paragraph. Now, while I am talking.
June: Did you save yours?
Ivy: I save mine every eleven seconds. It is not a system, it is a condition.
June: [gentle] A tidy condition. My files are named with numbers that stopped meaning anything long ago.
Ivy: The tidiest. There, it is saved, and nothing was lost tonight. Onward, softly.

segments.flavor: June reads the overnight forecast for Marlow Bay
segments.text:
June: [gentle] The overnight numbers for Marlow Bay. Nine degrees at the waterfront, seven by the archive doors.
Ivy: Seven. That explains the cardigan.
June: It explains a great deal. The archives are colder than the weather outside them.
Ivy: [whisper] They keep the paper happy, and the paper has never once thanked anybody for it.
June: Paper never does. Winds light, harbor quiet, a long grey calm until sunrise.
Ivy: Perfect weather for a slow song. Here is one.

segments.flavor: back-announce like a book placed gently back on the shelf
segments.text:
Ivy: Three songs in a row and not one of them raised its voice. That was the point.
June: The middle one had a door closing in it.
Ivy: [whisper] Somebody recorded that in a room with a door. I think about that often.
June: You think about it every time we play it.
Ivy: Every time. Now the three of them go back on the shelf, one at a time, in order.
June: [gentle] You could put them back in any order. Nobody is checking the shelf tonight.
Ivy: I am checking the shelf tonight.
June: Of course. Take your time; the next set is already leaning against the desk, waiting.

segments.flavor: a library object the station would sell you a better one of
segments.text:
Ivy: [whisper] The fountain on the second floor runs warm for eleven seconds, then turns cold and honest.
Ivy: Count to eleven. It is worth the wait, and so is this next one.

segments.flavor: Theo whispers in about the essay due at dawn
segments.text:
Theo: [whisper] Ivy. I did a bad thing. I wrote the conclusion before anything else.
Ivy: That is not a bad thing. That is a map.
Theo: It is four sentences and they are all very confident.
Ivy: Then follow them backwards until you meet the beginning. Go. The music will cover you.

segments.flavor: Ivy whispers one reminder — stand up
segments.text:
Ivy: [whisper] Stand up. Not for long. Just long enough for the chair to forget your shape.
June: How far is far enough?
Ivy: To the window and back. The window is eleven steps from most desks in here.
June: [gentle] And what is at the window?
Ivy: Nothing. Fog, a parked car, a light on in one other building.
June: Somebody else is up.
Ivy: Somebody else is always up. Sit down again slowly; the next song starts on the way back.

segments.flavor: June reads the overnight forecast for Marlow Bay
segments.text:
June: [gentle] The full overnight for Marlow Bay, since we have a moment and nobody is in a hurry.
Ivy: Take as long as you like.
June: Fog on the water until three. Then a thin wind from the east, tidying it away.
Ivy: [whisper] Tidying. I like that.
June: The ferry does not run any more, so the harbor has nothing to be woken by.
Ivy: Only the bell.
June: Only the bell, and it is polite about it. Inland, mild. The hill district stays dry.
Ivy: And the reading room?
June: [gentle] Warm, quiet, one lamp too bright in the corner. Twelve more minutes of music now.

segments.flavor: back-announce like a book placed gently back on the shelf
segments.text:
Ivy: [whisper] That last one goes back face up, because the cover is nicer than the title.
Ivy: There. Shelved. Now something with brushes on the drums and nowhere particular to be.

segments.flavor: a library object the station would sell you a better one of
segments.text:
Ivy: [whisper] The radiator under the north window sings one note all night, and it is slightly flat.
Ivy: We have stopped tuning around it. Consider it the oldest member of tonight's band. Play on.

segments.flavor: Theo whispers in about the essay due at dawn
segments.text:
Theo: [whisper] I have read the same paragraph nine times. It is a fine paragraph. It will not go in.
Ivy: Nine is the number where you stop. Close the book.
Theo: And then what?
June: [gentle] And then you say the paragraph out loud, badly, in your own words.
Theo: Badly is allowed?
Ivy: Badly is the door. Go on, Theo. Music for the walk back to the table.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a library product — wool socks for the stacks
segments.text:
June: [gentle] A short word from Cathedral Wool, makers of the Stack Sock, in grey and darker grey.
Ivy: Thick enough for a cold floor. Quiet enough for the third floor after midnight.
June: Wear them under boots, or instead of boots, if the night has gone that way.
Ivy: [whisper] No one can hear you cross a reading room in Stack Socks. Nobody ever has.
June: Cathedral Wool. Warm feet, clear head, no announcement.
Ivy: Sold in pairs, which is generous of them.
June: [whisper] Socks do not improve spelling. Results vary. Something slow next, please.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a library product — a pen with nothing to click
segments.text:
Ivy: [gentle] Study Hall is quiet tonight thanks to the Vesper Pen, the pen with nothing to click.
June: The cap comes off. That is the entire mechanism.
Ivy: No spring. No button. No small plastic sound at the end of every thought.
June: Ink is black, blue, or the blue that looks black under a lamp.
Ivy: The Vesper Pen. It will never give you away.
June: [whisper] Pen writes what it is told. Cap sold separately after you lose it. Music.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a library product — a door that closes slowly
segments.text:
June: [gentle] The Marlow Bay Hinge Company presents the Slow Return, a door closer for serious buildings.
Ivy: A door with the Slow Return takes nine seconds to close and makes no announcement.
June: Nine seconds is long enough for a coat, a bag, and an armful of books.
Ivy: [whisper] We have one on the east stairwell. It has never startled anybody.
June: The Slow Return. Because a door should end a sentence, not interrupt one.
Ivy: Installation requires a screwdriver and a friend.
June: [whisper] Company not liable for doors held open by furniture. Let the song back in.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a library product — a keyboard nobody can hear
segments.text:
Ivy: [gentle] The Featherstone Keyboard. Every key travels two millimetres and arrives without telling the room.
June: We tested it at the long table. Nobody looked up. Nobody ever looks up.
Ivy: The space bar is the quietest part, which is the part that gets hit hardest.
June: [gentle] It is beige. They did not have to do that, and yet.
Ivy: The Featherstone Keyboard. Type all night. Wake nobody.
June: [whisper] Keyboard does not improve the writing. Nothing does. Something gentle next.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a library product — a clock with no tick
segments.text:
June: [gentle] Now a word about the Quiet Hour, a wall clock with no tick whatsoever.
Ivy: The hands move. They simply do not comment on it.
June: Available in white, in cream, and in the shade libraries choose when nobody is watching.
Ivy: [whisper] It will still tell you it is late. It will just be kind about it.
June: The Quiet Hour. Time, without the small noise.
Ivy: Batteries last a year, which feels like a promise.
June: [whisper] Clock does not slow time. We asked. The next song, gently.

segments.flavor: the lost and found drawer, read aloud
segments.text:
Ivy: [gentle] Time for the drawer. The lost and found, read aloud, as we do.
June: One glove. Left hand. Good condition. Slightly hopeful.
Ivy: One set of keys with a wooden fish on the ring.
June: [gentle] A pressed leaf inside a book about tax law.
Ivy: Somebody was having a much better time than the book suggests.
June: One umbrella, dry, which means it has been here a while.
Ivy: [whisper] And a single earring that has outlasted three carpets.
June: The drawer stays open until dawn. Until then, music, and plenty of it.

segments.flavor: the stacks report
segments.text:
Ivy: [gentle] The stacks report, for anybody who has to go down there tonight.
June: Aisle four has the light that hums.
Ivy: Aisle seven has the light that does not come on at all until you give up.
June: [gentle] Then it comes on.
Ivy: Then it comes on, proudly, as if it had been working the whole time.
June: Aisle nine is cold. Aisle ten is colder and smells like old paper and rain.
Ivy: [whisper] Aisle ten is my favourite place in this building.
June: Of course it is. Take a lamp, take your time, and take this song with you.

segments.flavor: what the returns desk found inside the books
segments.text:
June: [gentle] The returns desk collected four books tonight, and three of them had something inside.
Ivy: A bus ticket, folded twice, used as a bookmark at page two hundred.
June: They got to page two hundred. That is a finished book, nearly.
Ivy: [gentle] A shopping list in the second one. Bread, batteries, something crossed out twice.
June: And the third?
Ivy: A note that says, keep going. No name. No date. Just that.
June: [gentle] We put it back where we found it, obviously.
Ivy: Page ninety. Somebody will need it. Here is a song that agrees with the note.

segments.flavor: the night shelf recommendation
segments.text:
Ivy: [whisper] The night shelf. One book, recommended quietly, with no obligation whatsoever.
June: What is on it?
Ivy: A thin book about lighthouses. Nobody has opened it since the shelf was built.
June: [gentle] Is it good?
Ivy: I have no idea. It has an excellent first page and I stopped there, twice.
June: That is a recommendation of a kind.
Ivy: [whisper] It is the only kind we give. It will be there tomorrow, and after.
June: Something with a lighthouse in it now, probably by accident.

segments.flavor: the hourly count of lamps still on
segments.text:
June: [gentle] Ivy does a count at this hour. She has done it for years.
Ivy: Fourteen lamps on. Nine desks in use. One kettle, cooling.
June: The kettle is not a person.
Ivy: [whisper] The kettle is doing more work than most people in this building tonight.
June: Fourteen is a good number. It was eight last week at this hour.
Ivy: Eight is a sad number. Fourteen is a room with something happening in it.
June: [gentle] Quietly happening.
Ivy: The best kind. That is the count. The music takes it from here.
